title: As robotaxi accidents increase in L.A., the data reveal the safer driver
key_facts: The Times reviewed autonomous-vehicle crash data filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA): accidents tied to Waymo tripled last year in Los Angeles County as it put more robotaxis on the road; most were fender benders.
Per the California Autonomous Vehicle Crash Dashboard (built by UC Berkeley's Matthew Raifman and colleagues), Waymo reported 186 crashes in LA County this year, 219 in 2025 and 69 in 2024.

This year 149 involved a passenger vehicle, 11 a heavy truck and 2 a first-responder vehicle; 82 happened while the Waymo was stopped and 65 while driving straight; just over 80% caused no apparent injuries, 15% possible injuries and fewer than 1% a suspected serious injury.
Statewide, more than 590 accidents involved Waymo robotaxis in California in 2025, nearly double the 304 in 2024.
Waymo-reported crashes per million miles fell from about 57 in 2023 to fewer than six this year; experts say the rise in crash counts is expected with more vehicles on the road.

Waymo says that across 67 million miles in Los Angeles it had zero crashes with serious or fatal injuries against 11 expected for human drivers; its safety researcher Kris Kusano says the data are 'quite conclusive' that the cars are safer than average drivers in the cities where they operate.

Caveats: experts warn the data reflect vehicles operating only in controlled environments with mild weather; skeptics say companies have an incentive to under-report or misclassify incidents; University of San Francisco researcher William Riggs says the best technology is safer than humans now but 'what we can't say' is whether the AV industry at large is.

Local response: San Diego's city council voted last month to ask the state for authority over when and how robotaxis are deployed (the state utilities commission currently governs it); Culver City voted to set rules on where fleets can be charged, stored and cleaned; Zoox has been in 18 California crashes this year per NHTSA data.
quote_evidence: Accidents tied to Mountain View, Calif.-based Waymo tripled last year in L.A. County as it put more robotaxis on the road.

Waymo has reported 186 crashes in Los Angeles County this year, 219 in 2025 and 69 in 2024, according to data compiled by the California Autonomous Vehicle Crash Dashboard built by Raifman and his colleagues.
Experts say the sharp increase in crashes shouldn’t immediately raise alarm — with more robotaxis on the road, they are bound to be involved in more incidents.
why_it_matters_hint: Robotaxis are spreading to more cities and crash counts are rising with fleet size, while the data so far cannot settle whether driverless cars are safer than human drivers overall, which is what residents and city officials are asking.
event_date: Analysis published 5 Oct 2026; crash data run to about this autumn (186 LA County crashes so far in 2026).
